metaDescription: Perimeter risk assessment, NDAA Section 889 compliance audit, and insurance optimization review. Senior engineers, not deck-only consultants.
announcementBar: Engineers, not deck-only consultants. Site visit included.
h1: Perimeter risk. NDAA compliance. Insurance posture. Three reports your CFO and CSO will both read.
heroSubhead: Senior security engineers walk your perimeter, audit your compliance posture, and benchmark your insurance terms. Deliverables are working documents with named recommendations and dollar figures — not pretty PDFs.
body:
The consulting market is full of slide decks that don't translate into action. We do consulting the way our SOC writes incident reports: named subjects, dollar figures, recommended next actions.

Three engagements. Each one stands alone or stacks into a complete security review.

## Perimeter Risk Assessment

A senior engineer spends a half-day to a full day on site. Walks the perimeter, photographs gaps, tests existing camera coverage, reviews access control logs, interviews the site supervisor and the local LE liaison.

Deliverable includes:
- Site map with current camera coverage, blind spots, and recommended additions
- Force-on-force scenarios: cut-fence, ram-vehicle, social-engineering, insider-threat
- Loss exposure model in dollars: tools, copper, switchgear, equipment, fuel, vehicles
- Lighting and natural-surveillance recommendations (some of which cost nothing)
- Recommended phasing: what to do in 30 days, 90 days, 12 months
- Vendor-neutral specification of what to procure — we'll tell you when VDS is the wrong fit

Typical engagement: $4,500–$9,500 depending on site size and travel. Credited toward managed services contract if you sign within 90 days.

## NDAA Section 889 Compliance Audit

Section 889 of the 2019 NDAA prohibits federal contractors and grant recipients from using covered telecom and video surveillance equipment from named manufacturers (Hikvision, Dahua, Hytera, Huawei, ZTE) or their OEM-rebranded variants.

Most facilities don't know what's installed. We do the audit:

- Physical inventory of every camera, NVR, switch, and access control device on site
- Firmware and chipset analysis on flagged devices (rebrands often hide upstream components)
- Documentation review: invoices, prior procurement records, manufacturer attestations
- Written remediation plan with prioritized replacement schedule
- Updated attestation letter for federal compliance officers

Audit findings have caught Section 889 violations at 41 of the 73 facilities we've audited since 2021. Most clients didn't know they were non-compliant.

Engagement runs 2–4 weeks. Pricing scales with device count: starts at $7,500 for under 50 devices, custom-quoted for enterprise.

## Insurance Optimization Review

Most commercial property and inland-marine policies offer premium credits for documented physical security measures. Most insureds never claim them because the carrier paperwork is opaque and the security vendor doesn't talk to the broker.

We do:
- Review current policy declarations, endorsements, and underwriting questionnaire
- Document existing security posture in carrier-readable format
- Coordinate with your broker on credit eligibility (theft, vandalism, business interruption, builder's risk)
- Model premium impact of incremental security investments
- Provide post-incident documentation packets if you have a claim history that's hurting your rates

Average documented premium savings on engagements completed in 2024: $18,400/year across mid-size accounts. Largest single savings: $94,000/year on a multi-site logistics account.

Engagement is $3,500–$6,500, typically completed in 3 weeks. We don't take broker commissions — we work for the insured.

## How the three stack

Most clients run the Perimeter Risk Assessment first because it produces immediate operational findings. The NDAA audit follows when there's a federal contract pending or a procurement review coming up. The Insurance Review goes last because the findings from the first two feed the carrier conversation.

Done together, the three deliverables form a security posture report that goes to the board with hard numbers attached.

## Who does the consulting

VDS senior engineers with 10+ years of physical security infrastructure experience. Backgrounds across DoD, federal LE, critical infrastructure, and commercial construction. Not third-party consultants. Not the SDR who quoted your trailer.

Engagements are billed flat-fee, not T&M. We don't pad hours.

faq.q: Are you a vendor or a consultant? Isn't this a conflict?
faq.a: Both. We disclose it up front. The consulting deliverables identify what to do — and explicitly call out when VDS is not the right vendor for a given line item. We've recommended competitors on roughly 1 in 8 engagements. Honest scope is the only way the consulting model works long-term.

faq.q: Will you sign an NDA before the engagement?
faq.a: Yes. Standard mutual NDA template available, or we'll sign yours after legal review. Findings remain customer property; we publish anonymized methodology only.

faq.q: How long does an NDAA audit take?
faq.a: Typical 50–200 device facility: 2–3 weeks from kickoff to written report. Larger enterprise environments: 4–8 weeks. Remote-only audits (documentation review without site visit) are 30–40% faster but catch less.

faq.q: Do you offer insurance review without the security work?
faq.a: Yes, as a standalone engagement. We don't take broker commissions, so the recommendation is vendor-neutral. About 30% of insurance reviews don't result in any VDS hardware sale — and that's by design.

faq.q: What if your assessment recommends a competitor?
faq.a: We say so in writing. We've recommended Genetec, Avigilon, and Verkada on specific engagements where their product fit the use case better than ours. The credibility of the consulting practice depends on this being real.

finalCTABody: 30-minute scoping call to confirm the right engagement. On-site work begins within 2 weeks. Written deliverable inside 3 weeks of the site visit.
notes: Expansion status — verify consulting capacity and bench depth before promoting heavily. Sample deliverable should be a real anonymized PDF gated by email.

seoTitle: Deployment Logistics | National Trailer Install & Redeploy
metaDescription: Site survey, transport, install, redeploy. Managed end-to-end across 30+ states. Same-day to 72-hour deployment. 500+ deployments completed.
heroSubhead: Site survey, transport, install, level, configure, redeploy. Same-day to 72-hour on most US locations. 500+ completed deployments across 30+ states.
heroStats: 30+ states • Same-day to 72-hour deployment • DOT-compliant transport • Insured fleet
body:
A trailer that sits in a yard is not security. Getting steel onto the dirt — on the right pad, at the right elevation, with the right view angles, levered up, leveled, and connected — is half the job. VDS runs deployment logistics as a single managed workflow from quote to operational.

## Phase 1: Site survey

Every deployment opens with a survey. Three formats depending on the engagement:

- **Remote desk survey** — satellite imagery, customer-provided site photos, address geocoding for cellular signal estimate. Same day, no charge. Sufficient for ~60% of deployments.
- **Drive-by survey** — regional tech visits the site for 30-60 minutes, captures RF measurements on all four carriers, photographs sight lines and ingress, confirms pad surface. 2-5 business days, no charge for serious-buyer engagements.
- **Full on-site survey** — 2-4 hour engagement with a senior solutions engineer. Coverage mapping per camera, mast height analysis, neighbor / nuisance considerations, lighting analysis for IR vs. visible. Quoted per site for complex deployments.

Deliverable: a site plan PDF with proposed camera positions, view fields, mast height, expected RF, and pad requirements.

## Phase 2: Pre-deployment

- Trailer prep at the regional staging facility — battery balance check, firmware update to current release, camera focus verification, SIM activation, AI rules pre-loaded
- Customer access coordination — gate codes, escort requirements, badging, insurance certificates
- Permits where required — most municipalities do not require permits for a trailer; some HOAs and a handful of city codes do. We handle the filing.

## Phase 3: Transport

Our fleet runs DOT-compliant CDL drivers across owned tractors and a vetted contract network. Transport insurance is $1M per load. Most metro markets are reached from a regional yard within an 8-hour drive window.

Typical timelines:

- **Same-day** — 60-mile radius from a regional yard, request received before 10am local
- **Next-day** — 250-mile radius, request received before 5pm local
- **72-hour** — anywhere in the continental US not already covered by the above

Hawaii, Alaska, and Puerto Rico are quoted separately; ocean freight adds 7-21 days.

## Phase 4: On-site install

Standard install runs 90-180 minutes per trailer:

1. Position and level — hydraulic outriggers, bubble level, 2-degree tolerance
2. Mast deployment — 12-30 ft typical, wind-rated to 75 mph deployed
3. Camera aim and focus — verified against the site plan via on-platform live view
4. Cellular antenna alignment — peaked for best RSRP on primary and secondary carriers
5. Solar panel orientation — magnetic south, tilt-adjusted for latitude
6. Configuration push — AI rules, retention policy, user permissions, alert routing
7. SOC handoff — operator confirms inbound stream, AI events firing, audio talk-down test
8. Customer walkthrough — site contact gets the portal login and a live demo on their site

A typical 4-camera install with a 2-person crew completes in under 2.5 hours.

## Phase 5: Redeploy

The most common operational request: move the trailer. New phase of a construction project, new event venue, seasonal retail, post-storm response.

Redeployment is treated as a fresh install — survey (usually remote for repeat customers), transport, level, reconfigure. Same crew network. 24-72 hour standard turnaround within a state, 5-7 days cross-country.

For multi-site customers with frequent rotations, we provision a regional swap inventory — a spare trailer staged within a few hours of the highest-rotation sites. Redeploys against the swap inventory take hours, not days.

## Coverage footprint

Active deployments today across all of the lower 48 except for Vermont and Wyoming. Eight regional yards positioned to keep transport drives under 8 hours for ~92% of US population centers. Field-tech network covers every market we deploy into.

## What is not included by default

- Concrete pad construction (most sites use the existing ground; gravel and packed dirt are fine)
- Power tie-in (trailers are solar-autonomous; AC power is optional for high-density camera builds)
- Long-term lease of customer-owned land — that is between the customer and the property holder

## What is included

Survey, transport, install, configure, monthly device health, redeploy at no transport surcharge for in-state moves under contract.

faq.q: How fast can you get a trailer to a new site?
faq.a: Same-day inside 60 miles of a regional yard. 72 hours anywhere in the continental US.

faq.a: No. Trailers are solar-autonomous with multi-carrier cellular included. Wired uplink and AC power are optional, never required.

faq.a: Gravel, dirt, packed soil, asphalt, concrete. Mud and standing water require gravel base or a steel mat we can provide.

seoTitle: Device Health Monitoring | Proactive Trailer Telemetry | VDS
metaDescription: 24/7 telemetry on battery, solar, cellular, camera uptime, and tamper. Failures predicted and dispatched before downtime
h1: Device Health Monitoring Before Failure, Not After
heroSubhead: Battery state, solar input, cellular RSRP, camera frame rate, and tamper status streamed to the VDS NOC every 60 seconds. Issues open a ticket before a camera goes dark.
heroStats: 60-second telemetry • 99.6% uptime SLA • Predictive battery alerts • Included with every trailer
body:
Every VDS trailer reports to our network operations center every 60 seconds. We monitor the things that actually fail on a remote outdoor unit — and we open the ticket before you find out about the outage from your facility manager.

## What we measure

**Power system**
- Battery voltage, current, and state-of-charge (SoC)
- Battery temperature (cold-soak risk in northern climates, thermal runaway risk in southern)
- Solar panel input voltage and current per string
- Charge controller mode (bulk, absorb, float, equalize)
- Daily kWh in vs. kWh out — predicts winter SoC drift before it becomes a brown-out

**Connectivity**
- Cellular RSRP, RSRQ, and SINR per modem
- Carrier and band attached (Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile, FirstNet)
- Failover events between primary and secondary SIM
- Starlink uplink throughput and obstruction percentage (where deployed)

**Cameras**
- ONVIF heartbeat per camera, 30-second interval
- Frame rate, bitrate, packet loss
- Lens fault (focus drift, condensation, obstruction detected via image analytics)
- IR illuminator current draw — predicts night-vision degradation

**Physical**
- Tilt sensor (trailer leveling drift, attempted tipping)
- Door / panel switches (cabinet access, attempted entry)
- GPS position vs. expected geofence
- Mast extension limit switches

## Alert thresholds, not just dashboards

A dashboard is not a service. We define thresholds per metric and per deployment context. A construction site in Phoenix in July gets different thermal limits than a logistics yard in Fargo in January. Default thresholds for the most common alerts:

- Battery SoC below 35% on a clear-sky day → ticket opened, solar diagnostic dispatched
- Cellular RSRP worse than -110 dBm for 15 minutes → ticket, antenna inspection
- Camera frame rate below 80% of nominal for 5 minutes → ticket, stream restart attempted automatically
- Tamper sensor triggered → SOC notified immediately, audio talk-down armed, dispatch evaluated
- GPS position outside geofence → escalation, vehicle recovery procedure

## What happens when an alert fires

1. NOC engineer acknowledges within 5 minutes during business hours, 15 minutes overnight
2. Remote diagnostics — firmware status, recent log review, attempt remote fix
3. If unresolvable remotely, dispatch decision: customer-fixable, regional tech, or trailer redeploy
4. Customer notified by email, SMS, or webhook depending on tenant preference
5. Resolution logged to the immutable audit trail

A typical fix-without-truck-roll rate across our fleet runs 73%. The remaining 27% generate a same-day to 72-hour field response depending on site criticality.

## Predictive replacement

Battery banks have a service curve. We track depth-of-discharge cycles and Peukert-adjusted capacity per pack and flag replacement at roughly 80% of expected end-of-life — typically months ahead of failure. Same for fan-cooled cellular modems, IR illuminators, and dome-camera gaskets.

## What the customer sees

A live dashboard per trailer with the same metrics we monitor, downloadable monthly health PDFs, and webhook subscription if you want the data piped into your own ITSM (see the API page). Uptime SLA is reported per quarter against a 99.6% target.

## Included, not upsold

Device health monitoring is included with every VDS-deployed trailer at no extra cost. We are responsible for keeping the asset online; this is the instrumentation that lets us hold ourselves to that.

faq.q: Does this apply to my own cameras on a VDS network?
faq.a: Camera health monitoring applies to any ONVIF-compliant camera on AI VisionStream, including yours. Trailer-specific telemetry (battery, solar) applies to VDS-owned trailers.

faq.q: What is the historical retention for health data?
faq.a: 12 months at full resolution, 5 years at hourly aggregates.

faq.q: How are tamper alerts validated to avoid false positives from animals or weather?
faq.a: Tamper is a composite signal: tilt + door switch + camera analytics + SOC visual confirmation. Single-sensor triggers escalate to human review before dispatch.

faq.q: Can I set custom alert thresholds?
faq.a: Yes. Tenant admins can override defaults per site or per device class.

faq.q: What is the cost?
faq.a: Included with every VDS trailer subscription. No separate line item.

finalCTABody: We will pull anonymized health data from a comparable deployment so you can see the dashboard, the alert flow, and the monthly report format.
notes: Anchor the 99.6% uptime number. Link from hardware page and from MSU buyer's guide.

heroSubhead: Permanent installs, mast-mounted fixed cameras, retrofits on existing infrastructure, and quarterly preventive maintenance. Licensed technicians in 30+ states. We service VDS hardware and cameras you already own.
body:
Most security failures aren't camera failures. They're install failures, mounting failures, and "no one cleaned the lens in two years" failures. We do the boring work that keeps the rest of it working.

## Permanent install

Mast-mount, building-mount, pole-mount, parking-deck mount. Concrete coring, conduit runs, weatherproofing, lightning arrest, and grounding to code. We pull permits where required and coordinate with your GC if you're on an active project.

What we install:
- VDS-branded fixed cameras and PTZ
- Third-party cameras you specified (Axis, Hanwha, Bosch, Hikvision-replacement programs, Verkada migrations)
- Mast extensions and parapet mounts
- Solar-only power kits for buildings without exterior conduit
- Cellular backhaul kits where running fiber isn't practical

## Retrofit on existing camera infrastructure

If you already have 40, 200, or 2,000 cameras, the install service that matters is the one that doesn't ask you to throw them away. Our VMS speaks ONVIF and RTSP — we connect to your existing infrastructure, add analytics and SOC monitoring, and only replace cameras when the math says replace.

Typical retrofit:
- Inventory audit of existing cameras, NVRs, and network
- ONVIF/RTSP connectivity test, firmware update on supported models
- Replace truly dead cameras (usually 5–15% of fleet)
- Cloud VMS cutover with side-by-side parallel operation
- SOC onboarding once analytics are tuned

Average retrofit cost is 12–18% of the cost of a full rip-and-replace.

## Preventive maintenance

Quarterly site visits on every camera under contract:
- Lens cleaning (the single highest-impact maintenance item)
- Housing seal inspection
- Mount torque check
- Cable continuity and PoE budget verification
- Firmware updates
- IR illuminator test
- Battery and solar health on mobile units
- DVR/NVR health check (where applicable)

Reports filed in the customer portal. Annual deep-service includes mast inspection, lightning arrest test, and full housing reseal.

## Redeployment

Construction sites change phases. Lay-down yards relocate. Substation outages end. When a perimeter shifts, the trailers and fixed-mast units move with it. Redeployment is included in managed contracts. For owned hardware, it's a flat-fee service call per unit.

## Emergency service

24/7 dispatch for client-down events. SOC sees a camera offline before you do — and dispatches our field tech with the customer's authorization. Average on-site response in metro markets: under 6 hours. Rural sites quoted per the field tech coverage map.

## Who does the work

W-2 field technicians, not 1099 contractors. Background-checked. OSHA-30 minimum. Tower-climber certified where height work is required. Insured under VDS general liability and workers' comp — your project doesn't carry the risk.

We subcontract only for trenching, electrical above 600V, and licensed crane work. Every subcontractor goes through our vendor compliance check.

faq.q: Will you service cameras VDS didn't sell us?
faq.a: Yes, with conditions. If the camera is in current manufacturer support and we can pull firmware and config, we service it. If it's end-of-life and parts are unobtainable, we'll quote replacement instead.

faq.q: Do you do tower climbing and high-mast work?
faq.a: Yes. Tower-climber certified techs for mast work up to 80 feet. Above that we coordinate with a partner crane crew. Quoted per project.

faq.q: What's the SLA on emergency service?
faq.a: Metro markets: on-site under 6 hours. Regional markets: under 12 hours. Rural: under 24 hours. Managed contracts include emergency response; standalone hardware service is billed T&M with a 2-hour minimum.

faq.q: Can you handle permitting and inspections?
faq.a: Yes for low-voltage and security trade permits. We coordinate with your GC for electrical and structural permits where required. We do not pull GC-of-record permits.

faq.q: What does a maintenance contract cost?
faq.a: Quarterly PM averages $40–$75 per camera per quarter depending on access difficulty and travel. Discounts for sites with 25+ cameras. Mobile trailers are bundled into managed service pricing.

finalCTAHeading: Get a site survey on the calendar.

heroSubhead: Everything in one contract. Trailers and cameras. 24/7 US SOC. Field service and PM. Monthly reporting. No capex. No surprise invoices. Cancel with 90 days notice.
body:
Capex is dead weight on a project budget. Multi-vendor opex is a finger-pointing exercise. Managed services from a vertically integrated provider is the only model that makes the math and the accountability work.

## What's included in the monthly fee

- Hardware (trailers, fixed cameras, mast units) — owned by VDS, deployed at your site
- 24/7 US SOC monitoring with full event response and LE dispatch
- Quarterly preventive maintenance on every camera
- Emergency field service inside SLA
- Redeployment as your site changes
- Monthly reporting: incident logs, dispatch records, false-alarm rates, camera uptime, recommendations
- Customer portal access for live video, recorded video, incident history, and event export
- VMS license and cloud storage at your contracted retention
- Cellular data and connectivity
- All firmware and software updates

One line item on the PO. One invoice per month. One escalation path.

## What's not included

- Capex on hardware (intentionally — you don't own it)
- Police response costs (handled by your jurisdiction)
- Insurance premiums (though our case study shows them dropping)
- Damage from intentional vandalism by authorized personnel (covered for unauthorized)

## The case study, in plain numbers

A $28M Mid-Atlantic mixed-use construction project, 14 months in scope.

Before VDS (guard service):
- $32,400/month for two 24/7 armed guards
- 14 reported theft incidents in the prior 12-month equivalent
- $186,000 in filed insurance claims for theft and vandalism
- Two guard-related incident reports requiring legal review

After 12 months on VDS Managed:
- $4,000/month
- 4 reported theft incidents (73% reduction)
- $0 insurance claims filed
- Zero legal-review incident reports

Net annual savings: $340,800. Theft losses prevented: estimated $140,000 (insurer's own actuarial model). Total economic benefit: ~$480,000 in year one.

Full case study including dispatch records, redeployment timeline, and the insurance carrier's underwriting memo is available under NDA.

## How the pricing works

Three components, blended into one monthly number:

1. **Hardware unit fee** — per trailer or per fixed-camera channel, per month. Includes the unit, install/redeploy, and PM.
2. **Monitoring fee** — per camera channel, per month. Covers SOC, incident reports, and LE coordination.
3. **Platform fee** — flat monthly. Covers VMS, cloud storage, customer portal, integrations.

Typical small site (1 trailer, 6 cameras): $2,800–$4,500/month all-in.
Typical mid-size construction (3 trailers, 18 cameras): $7,500–$11,000/month.
Typical enterprise multi-site (50+ cameras across locations): negotiated, volume tiers below standard pricing.

Term is month-to-month with a 90-day cancellation notice. Annual contracts get a 10% discount.

## Reporting that goes to your CFO, not just your security manager

Monthly report includes:
- Incident summary with severity classification
- Dispatch records and LE response codes
- False-alarm rate (with quarter-over-quarter trend)
- Camera uptime and PM completion
- Cost-avoidance estimate against prior security model
- Insurance posture notes
- Recommendations for next quarter

The cost-avoidance line is the one your CFO cares about. We publish it because we have the numbers to back it.

## When managed is wrong for you

Managed isn't always the right model. If you have:
- An existing capitalized security infrastructure with depreciation life remaining
- A federal contract requiring hardware ownership for clearance reasons
- A security team that wants direct console access and prefers to operate their own SOC

…then standalone hardware or hardware + monitoring without full management is the better fit. We sell that too.

faq.q: What happens to the hardware at the end of the contract?
faq.a: We remove it. The hardware is ours. If you want to buy it out at the end of term, we publish a depreciation schedule with the contract.

faq.q: Can we cancel if it isn't working?
faq.a: 90 days notice, no penalty. We're confident enough in the model to make it easy to leave. We've had four cancellations in 500+ deployments since 2017; three of them were project completions, one was an acquisition by a vendor who used a different system.

faq.q: How does the managed service handle insurance carrier requirements?
faq.a: We provide a security plan document to your carrier on request, including camera placement, monitoring SLA, response procedures, and SOC certifications. Several carriers offer premium credits for VDS-monitored sites. We'll coordinate with your broker.

faq.q: Can managed services replace our guard contract entirely?
faq.a: In most cases yes. In some cases (lobbies, badge desks, high-net-worth visitor management) a reduced guard presence plus VDS Managed is the right model — typically 1 guard instead of 4. We'll scope honestly.

faq.q: What's the contract length?
faq.a: Month-to-month with 90-day notice, or annual with a 10% discount. We don't do 3-year or 5-year contracts. If we can't earn the renewal, you shouldn't be stuck with us.

finalCTAHeading: See the managed quote against your current spend.

metaDescription: Multi-carrier cellular (Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile, FirstNet) with Starlink failover. Managed by VDS. No carrier contracts on your side.
heroSubhead: Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile, and FirstNet SIMs in every trailer. Starlink failover for remote sites. You never sign a carrier contract.
heroStats: 4 carriers per trailer • FirstNet for public safety • Starlink failover • 99.9% link availability
body:
A surveillance camera without a working uplink is just a heat source. We treat connectivity as a managed service because customers consistently told us they do not want to manage four carrier accounts, three different APNs, and a quarterly review of who got dropped where.

## What you get

Every VDS trailer ships with at least two cellular modems and four pre-activated SIMs:

- **Verizon** — broadest coverage in most rural and suburban markets
- **AT&T** — primary fallback in markets where Verizon density is poor
- **T-Mobile** — strong in dense urban and some highway corridors
- **FirstNet (AT&T Band 14)** — dedicated public-safety priority for law enforcement, fire, and EMS deployments

The router runs active-active load balancing across whichever two modems are pulling the strongest signal at install time. If signal degrades, the router fails over inside 30 seconds without dropping the video stream — the AI VisionStream edge unit buffers across the cutover.

## Starlink failover

For sites where cellular coverage is genuinely absent — remote construction, oil and gas pads, federal land, agricultural — we mount a Starlink dish on the trailer mast. Starlink runs as a tertiary uplink behind the cellular modems and engages automatically when both cellular paths fall below a usable RSRP.

Starlink-equipped trailers maintain link availability above 99.5% in coverage corners where the nearest cell tower is 18+ miles away. Obstruction percentage is monitored as part of device health and a tree-canopy alert opens a ticket for site adjustment.

## You do not see a carrier bill

Cellular and Starlink data are bundled into the monthly trailer subscription. No carrier contracts on your side, no APN setup, no IMEI registration, no overage surprises.

Default data allocation is 100 GB per trailer per month at 1080p H.265 — sufficient for full-time recording with AI inference on four cameras. Trailers running 8+ cameras or 4K streams are sized up at provisioning. Overages, if they happen, are absorbed by VDS up to a fair-use ceiling defined in the MSA.

## Why multi-carrier matters

We have run controlled coverage tests across 30+ states. Single-carrier deployments hit dead zones in roughly 18% of customer sites — usually inside warehouses, behind hill features, or at remote yards where the assumed carrier turned out not to be the strongest. Multi-carrier with automated failover takes that to under 2%.

We do not pretend a particular carrier is best everywhere. We pick the best two at install based on a drive-test or fixed-survey, then keep watching with telemetry.

## Public safety: FirstNet

For police, sheriff, fire, EMS, and emergency-management deployments, FirstNet provides preemptive priority on AT&T's network — Band 14 plus QPP across commercial bands. During major events (severe weather, civil unrest, large-venue surges) commercial traffic gets de-prioritized; FirstNet traffic does not. We provision FirstNet on eligible accounts as the primary cellular path.

## Security on the wire

- TLS 1.3 between edge unit and AWS
- IPsec available for customer-managed VPN integrations
- Private APNs available with Verizon and AT&T enterprise accounts on request
- No public-facing ports on the edge unit; all sessions are outbound-initiated

## Cellular signal mapping at install

Every site survey includes a live RF measurement on all four carriers. We deliver a one-page coverage report showing RSRP, RSRQ, and SINR per carrier so the customer knows what was measured, not just promised. If a site fails to meet a minimum-RSRP threshold on all four cellular paths, Starlink is added at our cost.

faq.a: Roughly 15-25 GB per camera per month at 1080p H.265 with 24/7 recording and AI analytics. We size the data plan to the camera count at provisioning.

faq.a: Yes, but most customers find it cheaper and simpler to ride on ours. Enterprise carrier accounts can be integrated on request.

faq.a: No. FirstNet eligibility is restricted to qualifying agencies and their extended primary users.

h1: 72 hours from signature to live feed.
heroSubhead: Solar-autonomous trailer on site, talking to our SOC, watching your perimeter — within three days of contract. No trenching. No permits. No utility tie-in. One person stages it in under 20 minutes.
body:
A trailer doesn't need a permit, a transformer, or a network drop. That's why we built one.

## What "72 hours" actually means

The clock starts at contract signature. Inside that window: deployment engineer reviews the site survey, the trailer is staged from one of our regional depots, freight is dispatched, our field tech meets the trailer at the gate, and the unit is online and talking to the SOC before the third sunset. We've hit this window on 96% of deployments since 2022. The misses were customer access issues — locked gates, missing site contacts.

## What's on the trailer

- **400W–800W solar array** sized for the latitude and tree canopy. Battery bank carries 5–7 days of overcast operation.
- **4–8 cameras** depending on perimeter geometry. PTZ + fixed combinations. 4K resolution. Thermal optional.
- **AI analytics on-board** for person/vehicle/loitering detection. Reduces uplink bandwidth and SOC false-alarm load.
- **Dual-carrier cellular** with automatic failover. Optional Starlink for remote sites.
- **Two-way audio** for SOC talk-down. 100dB+ SPL — audible across a 500-ft yard.
- **Strobe and floodlight** triggered manually by SOC or automatically by analytics.
- **Tamper sensors** on every access point. GPS lock. Theft recovery built in.

Assembled in Pikesville, MD. NDAA Section 889 compliant. Documentation ships with the unit.

## Setup in under 20 minutes

The trailer arrives on a standard goose-neck. Drop it, level it, raise the mast (electric), point the solar array south. The unit boots, registers with our cloud, and the SOC sees the feed inside ten minutes of mast-up. No ladders. No specialty tools. One person.

We've trained customer site supers to stage their own units in 18 minutes. Most clients let our field tech handle the first deployment and then self-service from there.

## Where it gets used

- **Active construction sites** — perimeter live before fencing is complete
- **Lay-down yards and material staging** — copper, switchgear, conduit
- **Port terminals and intermodal yards** — gate cameras and cargo perimeter
- **Utility substations** — temporary coverage during outage work
- **Disaster response** — FEMA staging, post-storm asset protection
- **Events and venues** — concerts, festivals, sporting facilities
- **Government and federal** — NDAA-compliant temporary perimeters
- **Cannabis cultivation and dispensary** — exterior perimeter and parking

## How it pays for itself

A two-guard 24/7 contract runs $28,000–$35,000/month in most metros. Two VDS trailers with SOC monitoring runs $3,500–$5,500/month. The Mid-Atlantic case study cut a $32,400 monthly bill to $4,000 and reduced theft 73% in the first year. The hardware pays itself back inside the first quarter on most projects.

## What we need from you

- Site address and gate access plan
- Single point of contact with phone and email
- One photo per camera location (phone photos are fine)
- Local law enforcement non-emergency number (we register the site)

That's it. The site survey, RF check, solar exposure analysis, and camera layout — we do those.

faq.q: What happens if the solar array doesn't get enough sun?
faq.a: The battery bank is sized for 5–7 days of zero solar input. If a site shows persistent shading on the survey, we add a second array, swap in a hybrid generator, or wire to local power. The SOC alerts on low-battery state 48 hours before it becomes a problem.

faq.q: How does it handle no cellular coverage?
faq.a: Dual-carrier cellular covers most sites — we run on whichever carrier wins the RF check. For genuinely dark sites we add Starlink. Latency to SOC stays under 400ms.

faq.q: Can you redeploy a trailer mid-project as the site changes?
faq.a: Yes. Redeployment is included in managed contracts. Hook up, tow, drop, re-level. Our field tech does it in two hours or trains your team.

faq.q: What's the rental vs. purchase model?
faq.a: Most clients rent under a managed services contract — hardware, monitoring, and maintenance bundled monthly. Purchase is available for clients who want capex ownership; SOC monitoring is a separate per-trailer subscription.

faq.q: Is the trailer tamper-proof?
faq.a: Tamper-resistant, not tamper-proof. Every access door has sensors. The mast locks. GPS reports continuously. We've had three theft attempts in 500+ deployments — recovered all three within 24 hours.

finalCTABody: 30-minute call, site survey within 48 hours, trailer on the ground inside 72 hours of signature. We start the clock when you do.

h1: Remote Video Monitoring for 24/7 Commercial Site Security
body:
Remote video monitoring turns camera systems into an operational security program. Instead of reviewing footage after an incident, your team gets real-time visibility, verified alerts, defined escalation, and evidence-ready reporting—so events are detected faster and handled consistently. Whether you’re protecting one location or managing multiple sites, remote monitoring helps reduce after-hours risk and makes response more consistent across your operation.



## The Command Center for Remote Video Monitoring

This platform connects cameras, monitoring workflows, and analytics into one operating view. Review events in real time, apply site rules to reduce noise, and generate evidence-ready reports for internal follow-up, claims, or investigations.

Live video access and playback

Smart alerts based on site rules

Verified response workflows

Incident reporting and exports

Multi-site visibility and user roles



## How Remote Video Monitoring Works



### Step 1: Coverage Planning for Risk Zones

Monitoring starts with a coverage plan that prioritizes the places incidents actually happen:

Entrances and exits

Perimeters and low-visibility edges

Drive lanes and chokepoints

Loading zones and service corridors

High-value storage areas

Known problem corners (repeat incident zones)

A good plan prevents blind spots and avoids the common mistake of relying on one wide-angle camera to cover everything.



### Step 2: Site Rules That Match Your Operations

Next, you define your site rules so monitoring is focused and actionable. Examples include:

After-hours access in restricted zones

Loitering in specific areas

Vehicle activity in closed lots

Access outside approved windows

Repeated activity patterns in known risk zones

This is how you reduce false alarms: focus on what matters during the hours it matters.



### Step 3: Detection and Alerting

Detection is configured to match your site rules and environment. Depending on your deployment, this can include:

Schedule-based zone alerting

Rules-based triggers tied to risk zones

Analytics-assisted detection where appropriate

The goal is fewer alerts with higher confidence, not constant motion notifications.



### Step 4: Verification and Escalation

When activity is detected, the workflow verifies what’s happening and follows the escalation path you define. A complete escalation plan answers:

What triggers an alert

Who is notified

How escalation happens (call, dispatch, on-site response)

What gets documented (clips, timestamps, notes, actions)



### Step 5: Incident Reporting and Evidence Retrieval

Monitoring is only useful if outcomes are documented. Each verified incident should produce:

A timestamped clip

A clear summary of what occurred

The response actions taken

Reporting your team can use for follow-up, claims, or investigations



## Who Remote Video Monitoring Is For

Remote video monitoring is for organizations that need after-hours coverage, consistent escalation, and evidence-ready reporting—especially when incidents repeat in the same zones or across multiple locations. If your current setup produces footage but not response, this service is built to close that gap.



### Best-fit teams and sites

Property managers and retail operators with recurring parking lot incidents, disputes, or after-hours activity

Shopping centers and malls where liability, pedestrian traffic, and multiple perimeter edges make response consistency critical

Construction teams needing coverage during early phases and after-hours when theft risk spikes

Logistics yards and warehouses with perimeter exposure, high-value inventory, and restricted zones

Public safety and municipal programs that require repeatable escalation protocols and reporting

Multi-site operations leaders who need standardized oversight, reporting, and user access control across locations



### Best-fit triggers

Incidents happen after-hours or in low-visibility zones

You have repeat problems in the same corners/rows/entry points

Your team can’t consistently watch cameras, and alerts are too noisy

You need documented incident reports for claims, investigations, or accountability



## What You Get: Service and Platform Capabilities

Remote video monitoring works best when the service layer and platform layer work together.

Service Layer:

Monitoring workflows aligned to your site rules

Verification steps that reduce noise and improve actionability

Escalation paths tailored to your response preferences

Consistent incident reporting and follow-up documentation

Ongoing tuning based on real incident patterns

Platform Layer:

Live video access and fast event review

Alerting tied to zones and schedules

Event logs with timestamps and case-style summaries

Multi-site visibility and role-based access controls

Evidence exports designed for real incidents



## Key Features of Our Remote Video Monitoring Service



### Verified response workflows

Site rules + verification reduce noise so escalation is consistent and actionable.



### Real-time alerting built around risk zones

Focus monitoring on entrances, perimeters, loading zones, and high-risk corners.



### Incident reporting with evidence-ready exports

Generate timestamped clips and summaries for investigations and claims.



### Multi-site oversight and standardization

Centralize visibility and apply consistent escalation and reporting across locations.



### Configurable monitoring windows

Monitor after-hours, weekends, or 24/7 depending on when your risk occurs.



### Integration support for existing systems

Maintain continuity with existing camera systems and operational workflows.



## Benefits of Remote Video Monitoring

Remote monitoring is designed to improve outcomes, not just capture footage:

Faster time-to-awareness during after-hours incidents

Improved deterrence when response is predictable

Reduced repeat incidents in known zones

More usable evidence for claims and investigations

Less manual effort reviewing video and chasing alerts

Consistent accountability across teams and locations



## Where Remote Video Monitoring Works Best



### Construction Sites

Construction risk often peaks early and after-hours. For fast coverage without waiting on permanent infrastructure, pair monitoring with mobile surveillance trailers to watch perimeters, entrances, equipment storage, and access points that shift by phase.



### Parking Lots and Retail Properties

Parking lots are exposed environments where incidents often happen at night and in low-visibility corners. Monitoring performs best when it’s built on a parking lot surveillance cameras coverage plan that reduces blind spots and produces evidence-ready incident clips.



### Shopping Centers

Shopping centers add complexity with multiple edges, service corridors, and repeat problem zones. Shopping center remote monitoring is valuable because it standardizes escalation and reporting for operational accountability across the property.



### Logistics Yards and Warehouses

Yards combine perimeter exposure and high-value inventory, which makes after-hours activity especially costly. Monitoring works best when it enforces restricted zones and produces consistent incident reports; use the same workflows across sites to keep response repeatable.



### Public Safety and Municipal Deployments

Temporary deployments and public-sector environments often require defined escalation protocols and repeatable reporting. Remote monitoring helps create a consistent response model and documentation trail for events, corridors, and critical infrastructure



## Service Levels, Procurement, and Support

Remote video monitoring scope typically depends on:

Number of sites and critical zones

Monitoring window (after-hours vs 24/7)

Escalation expectations and contacts

Reporting requirements and cadence

Integration needs and user roles

If procurement is part of the process, align early on purchase structure and program duration.



## Remote Video Monitoring FAQs

What is remote video monitoring?

Remote video monitoring is a service that uses defined site rules and response workflows to detect, verify, escalate, and document security events consistently.

Do I need 24/7 remote video monitoring?

Not always. Many commercial sites monitor during high-risk windows like after-hours and weekends. The best model depends on incident timing and staffing realities.

What happens when suspicious activity is detected?

The workflow typically includes detection, verification, escalation to your response path, and an incident report with timestamped evidence.

How does remote monitoring reduce false alarms?

By focusing on risk zones, applying schedule-based rules, including verification steps, and tuning the workflow to real site conditions.

Can remote monitoring work across multiple sites?

Yes. Multi-site oversight is one of the strongest use cases because escalation and reporting become standardized.

Can remote video monitoring be paired with mobile surveillance trailers?

Yes. Monitoring pairs well with rapid deployment coverage for temporary risk periods and evolving sites.



## Why Vision Detection Systems for Remote Video Monitoring

Vision Detection Systems is the remote video monitoring solution that connects cameras, alerts, analytics, and incident reporting into one operating view—so teams can verify events faster, escalate response consistently, and manage security across sites without jumping between tools.

Unified control over hardware, analytics, and monitoring workflows in one platform

Scalable from a single site to multi-site and nationwide operations

Reliable performance backed by 24/7 U.S.-based support for operational continuity

If you’re using remote video monitoring to reduce after-hours incidents and improve response, Vision Detection Systems helps standardize how events are detected, verified, documented, and reported—so outcomes are repeatable across every location.

body:
If a security vendor tells you their system only works with their cameras, they're selling lock-in, not security. We're not in that business.

## Camera-agnostic VMS

Our VMS ingests any camera that speaks ONVIF Profile S (live video) or Profile T (metadata and events), plus standard RTSP streams in H.264 and H.265. That covers Axis, Hanwha, Bosch, Sony, Pelco, Hikvision-replacement brands, Verkada exports, Avigilon ONVIF mode, and most consumer-grade cameras with RTSP enabled.

What you get from the cameras you already own:
- Cloud VMS with 30/60/90-day retention tiers
- AI analytics layer (person, vehicle, loitering, line-cross, abandoned object)
- SOC monitoring at the same SLA as VDS hardware
- Mobile and web clients with role-based access
- Audit trail and export for legal hold

## Access control integration

Bi-directional integration with the major ACS platforms:

- **Genetec Security Center** — synchronized event timeline, badge-to-video, door-forced-open with video clip attachment
- **Lenel OnGuard** — event ingest, alarm correlation, video-on-card-read
- **AMAG Symmetry** — full event sync
- **Avigilon Access Control** — native event bridge
- **Brivo, Kisi, Verkada Access** — cloud-to-cloud REST integration
- **Open Supervised Device Protocol (OSDP)** readers — direct ingest on hardware integrations

We provide the SOC operator the badge holder photo and access log inline with the video event. Door propped open at 2 a.m. with the wrong badge ID? Operator sees the video, the badge holder photo, and the door history on one screen.

## Alarm panel integration

UL-listed central station receiver. We ingest from Bosch, DMP, Honeywell, Napco, and DSC panels over IP, dialer, or cellular. Alarm signals are correlated with video at the SOC — every signal gets visual verification before LE dispatch.

## ITSM and ticketing

- ServiceNow — incidents auto-created for camera offline events, with run-of-show fields populated
- Jira Service Management — same
- Freshservice, Zendesk — REST webhook into ticket creation

Closed-loop workflow: SOC opens a ticket on a camera health event, field tech updates it from mobile during service, customer sees status without a phone call.

## ERP and accounting

- SAP — purchase order and asset tag integration for capex hardware
- Oracle Fusion — same
- NetSuite — billing reconciliation for managed services

Where it matters: the camera asset tag on the trailer matches the line item on the SAP PO matches the lease entry on the GL. Audit-clean from day one.

## How an integration project runs

Week 1 — Scoping call with your IT, security, and operations leads. Inventory audit. API access provisioning.

Week 2 — Sandbox integration in a non-production environment. SSO setup (SAML 2.0, OIDC). Role mapping.

Week 3 — User acceptance testing. Operator training on the merged console.

Week 4 — Production cutover. Side-by-side parallel for 30 days before decommissioning legacy.

Most integrations close inside 30 days. Complex multi-system integrations run 60–90 days with milestones.

## Security of the integration itself

SAML 2.0 / OIDC SSO. SCIM provisioning. API tokens scoped per integration and rotated quarterly. All API traffic over TLS 1.3. Audit logs exportable to your SIEM (Splunk, Datadog, Sentinel). SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA.

faq.q: Do you charge per integration?
faq.a: Standard integrations (Genetec, Lenel, ServiceNow, the major ACS platforms) are included in the VMS license. Custom integrations against a private API are quoted as professional services — typically 40–120 engineering hours.

faq.q: Can you integrate with our SIEM or SOAR?
faq.a: Yes. Event export to Splunk, Datadog, Sentinel, QRadar, and Chronicle via syslog or HTTPS webhook. SOAR playbook triggers via REST API.

faq.q: What about cameras that don't speak ONVIF?
faq.a: If they speak RTSP, we ingest them. If they speak neither — typically older proprietary systems — we recommend an NVR-side bridge or a camera replacement. We don't force replacement when the bridge works.

faq.q: Will adding the analytics layer break our existing VMS?
faq.a: No. We can run as the primary VMS, as a secondary cloud archive, or in parallel during a migration. Most retrofits start in parallel for 60 days.

faq.q: Where is customer data stored?
faq.a: AWS US-East and US-West by default. AWS GovCloud available for federal and CJIS workloads. Customer chooses region during onboarding. Data residency contracts available.

seoTitle: Video Retrieval Service | Chain of Custody | VDS SOC
metaDescription: SOC-managed video retrieval. Law enforcement requests, insurance evidence, internal investigations. SHA-256 chain of custody, secure portal delivery.
h1: Managed Video Retrieval With Chain of Custody
heroSubhead: Customer or law-enforcement evidence request comes in. The VDS SOC pulls the clip, validates the chain of custody, and delivers via a signed portal link.
heroStats: <60-minute median turnaround • SHA-256 hashed exports • Court-admissible chain of custody • 12-month immutable log
body:
Pulling video for evidence is a process, not a button. The wrong workflow — wrong timestamp, missing hash, ambiguous custodian — turns useful footage into something a defense attorney can challenge or an insurer can reject. The VDS SOC handles retrieval as a managed service so the chain stays intact.

## Two paths in

**Customer-initiated retrieval** — a manager, loss prevention officer, or risk team member opens a ticket through the portal, email, or phone. We need: site, approximate time window, what happened or what is being looked for. Response: median 30 minutes for standard requests during business hours, 90 minutes overnight.

**Law-enforcement-initiated retrieval** — an investigating officer calls our SOC line, provides agency, case number, and warrant or subpoena if applicable. We confirm the customer's release authorization policy on file, pull the clip, and deliver direct to the agency portal or evidence intake system. The customer is copied on the audit trail.

For active emergencies (in-progress incident, exigent circumstances), the SOC can authorize same-call release under the customer's pre-signed law-enforcement authorization. Most law-enforcement customers and many commercial customers maintain a standing release; the form is one page.

## What "chain of custody" actually means here

Every export carries a chain-of-custody manifest:

- Source camera ID and site ID
- Source timestamp range (UTC and local)
- SOC operator who generated the export
- Generation timestamp
- SHA-256 hash of the exported file
- AWS region of origin
- Audit log reference for the underlying source recording
- Recipient (customer user, law enforcement agency, insurer)
- Delivery method and timestamp

The manifest is a signed PDF generated by the platform and is reproducible on demand from the immutable 12-month audit log. If anyone asks "are you sure this is the original clip" — yes, and here is the hash to prove it.

## Delivery

Three options, customer chooses at tenant provisioning:

- **Signed portal link** — recipient downloads through HTTPS with TLS 1.3, link expires in 72 hours by default, single-recipient
- **Direct evidence-system integration** — Axon Evidence.com, NICE Investigate, Genetec ClearID, Motorola CommandCentral; we push the file with manifest attached
- **Physical media** — encrypted USB shipped by courier, used rarely for very large exports or air-gapped agencies

All deliveries are logged. The original source video is not deleted; the export is a copy, the source remains in retention until its retention policy expires.

## Common request types

- Workplace incident investigations (HR, EHS)
- Theft, shrinkage, internal loss prevention
- Slip-and-fall and other premises liability
- Auto incidents at logistics yards
- Construction safety incidents and OSHA recordable review
- Vandalism, trespassing, criminal mischief
- Law-enforcement support for outside-property crime where our cameras captured a vehicle or person of interest

## What the SOC operator actually does

1. Validate the requester against the authorization matrix
2. Identify the correct camera(s) by site and time
3. Frame the export window with appropriate pre-roll (default 60s) and post-roll
4. Preview the clip — confirms the right incident is captured, flags any privacy-sensitive content for redaction
5. Generate the export with manifest
6. Deliver via the chosen channel
7. Log every step to the audit trail

Median operator handle time on a clean request: 12 minutes. Median end-to-end customer turnaround: under 60 minutes.

## Privacy and redaction

For requests crossing jurisdictions with privacy obligations (HIPAA-adjacent healthcare, GDPR for international subsidiaries, state biometric laws), the SOC can request a redaction pass — face blur, license plate blur, or audio mute — before delivery. Redactions are reversible internally for court-ordered un-redaction but the delivered file is the redacted version with a separate hash.

## Pricing

Standard retrieval is included with every AI VisionStream tenant up to 25 requests per site per month. Higher-volume tenants and certified evidence integrations are priced separately. Law-enforcement support for customer-authorized agencies is always at no additional cost.

faq.q: How fast can I get a clip for an active incident?
faq.a: Inside 30 minutes during business hours, 90 minutes overnight, faster for active emergencies under pre-signed authorization.

faq.q: Do you support body-worn or dashcam footage?
faq.a: No. AI VisionStream and VDS retrieval cover fixed and trailer-mounted cameras. We integrate with Axon Evidence for handoff of related body-cam footage to investigators.

faq.q: Will my footage hold up in court?
faq.a: With the chain-of-custody manifest, SHA-256 hash, and immutable audit log reference, yes — our exports have been admitted in criminal proceedings in multiple jurisdictions. We do not provide expert testimony but the manifest is structured to support it.

faq.q: Who can authorize a release to law enforcement?
faq.a: Whoever your tenant admin designates in the authorization matrix. Most customers list 2-4 named individuals plus a 24/7 emergency standing release.

faq.q: Can law enforcement search my footage themselves?
faq.a: No. All retrieval goes through the VDS SOC. Law enforcement does not receive direct platform access without an explicit customer grant.

finalCTABody: SOC line is staffed 24/7. Existing customers, call the SOC. New customers, talk to us about adding video retrieval as part of a managed deployment.
